messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — onboarding Suzaku-7B (Mistral-style arch) into our int4 pipeline and hit odd emoji/embedding diffs across backends. Repro steps below. Anyone seen emoji normalization causing proj-order misalignment? :thinking:

alex: repro (minimal):
```bash
python export_onnx.py --model suzaku-7b --dtype fp16 --export onnx
python quantize.py --input suzaku.onnx --format int4 --scheme awq
python run_infer.py --onnx suzaku_int4.onnx --prompt "I ❤️ pizza"
```

alex: FP16 run matches reference logits. Int4 export yields shifted embedding projection and the emoji token gets split differently (\u201cI \u2764\ufe0f pizza\u201d vs \u201cI ❤️ pizza\u201d). Logs: 
```
# int4 run token ids: [72, 6534, 4, 102]
# fp16 run token ids: [72, 12879, 4, 102]
# embedding dot diff (first dim): 0.002 -> 0.14
```

alex: initial hypothesis: quantization reorder or a proj-weight permute during export that only shows up for tokens with multi-codepoint emoji.

@tanya: can you paste the tokenizer config and the onnx graph node names?

alex: tokenizer.json excerpt: `normalizer: {"name": "unicode_nfkc"}, pretokenizer: {"split": "whitespace"}, special_tokens: {"emoji_handling": "char"}`.

alex: ONNX nodes: `embed.weight`, `proj_attn.q_proj`, `proj_attn.k_proj`, `proj_attn.v_proj`, and a node `permute_proj_axes` added by our quantizer.

zach: hmm permute_proj_axes is our quantizer shim. It was added to try to align Gemma/Mistral proj orders. Could be buggy for odd head layouts. Which head layout is Suzaku using?

alex: Suzaku uses hetero-heads: some heads are 64-dim, some 48-dim due to legacy adapter. That might interact badly with a flat permute assuming uniform head_dim.

maria: interesting — emoji tokenization differences could come from NFKC normalization + byte-level tokenizer mapping. If the quantizer inserts a permute before embedding projection, the byte boundaries change and produce different ids.

ci-bot: [test-run] suzaku_int4_infer — failed (tokenization mismatch) — https://ci.internal/runs/3321

tanya: can you run a FP16->int4 roundtrip but keep the permute step disabled? maybe fallback to per-head slices instead of batch permute.

alex: tried that: `--quant-skip-permute` gave matching token ids to FP16 but logits still slightly off for multi-codepoint emojis. So two issues: tokenization mapping and weight quant rounding causing small dot-product shifts amplified by tokenizer difference.

zach: for the head-dim heterogeneity we should avoid a global reshape. I propose a small patch: when head_dims are nonuniform, quantizer emits per-head `reshape+transpose` with explicit offsets. I'll open a PR.

maria: also add a tokenizer hook to collapse emoji to a single codepoint pretokenize stage for our evals. That will catch the NFKC->byte mismatch. Could be added as a compatibility shim for Suzaku onboarding.

alex: patch idea sounds good. I also gathered a short bench: 50 prompts with emoji-heavy text. FP16 vs int4 w/o permute: accuracy drop 0.6% on generation BLEU; with permute incorrectly applied: 3.8% drop and token id mismatches.

tanya: please attach the minimal reproducer and the failing CI run in the PR. Label it `onboard/suzaku` and `quant/permute-fix`.

zach: note — we should audit other models with hybrid head dims (list from model registry) and mark them to skip global permute until we land more robust transform. I'll add a checklist in the PR.

alex: thanks. I'll also try converting with `transform_weights.py --per-head` and post a small diff of the proj axis order. If that matches FP16, then we're confident it's the permute step.

maria: one more: add a token-normalization unit test for multi-codepoint emoji — we've missed that before.

alex: all right creating PR now. summary: cause = quantizer permute assuming uniform head_dim + tokenizer NFKC mapping edge-case on emoji; mitigation = per-head permute + tokenizer pre-normalize shim + CI test. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: created issue #4781 for tokenizer test coverage.

tanya: awesome. ping me once PR is up and I'll coordinate a canary run on Dedicated.

zach: follow-up: we should also check K/V cache indexing correctness after per-head permute — will add a note.

alex: noted. thanks team.
